requirements.quote: On receiving a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, an endpoint MUST respond by echoing the data contained in the PATH_CHALLENGE frame in a PATH_RESPONSE frame.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PATH_RESPONSE frame containing an exact echo of the data from the received PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inject a PATH_CHALLENGE frame and verify that the endpoint sends a PATH_RESPONSE whose data matches the challenge data exactly.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT delay transmission of a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame unless constrained by congestion control.
requirements.condition: An endpoint has a packet containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame ready for transmission and congestion control does not constrain transmission.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Delay transmission of the packet for a reason other than congestion control.
requirements.why_checkable: Instrumentation can determine whether a ready PATH_RESPONSE packet is delayed and whether congestion control was constraining transmission at that time.

requirements.quote: A PATH_RESPONSE frame MUST be sent on the network path where the PATH_CHALLENGE frame was received.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a PATH_RESPONSE for a received PATH_CHALLENGE.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the PATH_RESPONSE on the same network path on which the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE was received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the PATH_RESPONSE on a different network path.
requirements.why_checkable: A multipath test can identify the ingress path of a PATH_CHALLENGE and compare it with the egress path of the corresponding PATH_RESPONSE.

requirements.quote: This requirement MUST NOT be enforced by the endpoint that initiates path validation, as that would enable an attack on migration; see Section 9.3.3.
requirements.condition: An endpoint initiated path validation and evaluates the received PATH_RESPONSE.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Require the PATH_RESPONSE to have arrived on the same network path on which the PATH_CHALLENGE was sent as a condition of accepting the validation response.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can initiate validation, return the matching PATH_RESPONSE through a different observable path, and verify that the initiator does not enforce same-path receipt.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST expand datagrams that contain a PATH_RESPONSE frame to at least the smallest allowed maximum datagram size of 1200 bytes.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a datagram containing a PATH_RESPONSE frame, and expansion to 1200 bytes would not cause the datagram to exceed the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Expand the datagram to a size of at least 1200 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the datagram at a size below 1200 bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The general 1200-byte expansion rule and its adjacent anti-amplification exception can be combined and checked by observing the datagram size and current amplification allowance.

requirements.quote: However, an endpoint MUST NOT expand the datagram containing the PATH_RESPONSE if the resulting data exceeds the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.condition: Expanding a datagram containing a PATH_RESPONSE would cause the resulting data to exceed the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Send without performing the otherwise required expansion.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Expand the datagram beyond the anti-amplification limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish a known anti-amplification allowance and verify that padding or other expansion is not applied when it would exceed that allowance.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame in response to one PATH_CHALLENGE frame; see Section 13.3.
requirements.condition: An endpoint is responding to a single PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send more than one PATH_RESPONSE frame attributable to that PATH_CHALLENGE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver one PATH_CHALLENGE and count the PATH_RESPONSE frames generated in response, requiring the count not to exceed one.
